apps.title: Project Takeover
apps.body: Taking over an existing project? Noesis shows its architecture, dependencies, and business logic from day one, cutting ramp-up time from weeks to days.

apps.title: Delivering Documented Software
apps.body: Ship documentation together with the software. Noesis generates it from the code, so what the client receives matches what was built.

apps.title: Architecture Audit/Review
apps.body: Review an architecture with the whole system in front of you. The map makes technical debt and problematic dependencies visible.

apps.title: Requirements Preparation
apps.body: See what the system does today before writing requirements. Noesis describes technical constraints in terms business stakeholders can read.

apps.title: Refactoring Planning
apps.body: See what a change will touch before you make it. The map shows the dependencies, so you can plan a migration step by step.

apps.title: Knowledge Transfer
apps.body: Documentation generated from code stays current as the codebase changes, so knowledge doesn't leave with the people who had it.

faq.q: Can Noesis handle multiple repositories for my libraries and microservices?
faq.a: Yes. Noesis scans multiple repositories and combines them into one consistent model of the whole system.

faq.q: Does it hallucinate like other AI tools?
faq.a: No. We build answers from deterministic code graphs first, then enrich with AI, so every fact is traceable.

faq.q: Isn't it easy to replace Noesis with pure AI-based solution?
faq.a: LLMs can’t guarantee the same result from one scan to the next, and running them over a whole codebase again and again gets expensive. Noesis does the structural analysis deterministically and uses AI only where it adds value, so results are repeatable, cheaper, and traceable back to the code.
Yes. We currently primarily support the on‑prem deployment model; your code never leaves your environment.

pillars.title: Precise System Map Creation
pillars.body: Static code analysis extracts the system map according to the P3 model: the Domain, Technology, and People perspectives and the relationships between them. P3 covers the essential concepts of software development and system architecture, which keeps the map readable.

pillars.title: AI-Enhanced Element Descriptions
pillars.body: Once the map structure is in place, AI writes descriptions of its elements. The descriptions build on the deterministic relationships, so both business stakeholders and development teams can read what each component does.

pillars.title: Comparable & Repeatable Analysis
pillars.body: Scan the same code twice and you get the same result. That lets you track architectural changes over time and compare scans, which AI-only tools can't guarantee.

pillars.title: Cost-Optimized AI Usage
pillars.body: The critical parts of the analysis run as inexpensive static code analysis. AI is applied only where it adds value, so you stay in control of the cost.
